turns.content: Thirteen identical point charges each have charge 2e. One is fixed at the centre P, and the other twelve lie on a sphere of radius 2 m. Write the electrostatic potential energy as k(2e)^2 times a geometric sum over distinct pairs.
Calculate the contribution to the geometric sum from the twelve centre-to-outer pairs.

Identify the minimum-energy arrangement of the twelve outer particles under the geometry established above and compute their outer-outer sum of 1/r_ij from the distinct pair separations and multiplicities, rather than using a tabulated continuum result.
Combine the two geometric contributions obtained above to form the minimized sum for all distinct pairs.
Calculate the SI prefactor implied by the interaction model established above, using the supplied constants k=8.9875517923e9 N m^2 C^-2 and e=1.602176634e-19 C.
Multiply the geometric sum by that prefactor and report the resulting minimum quantity in the SI units implied above, to three decimals in scientific notation.
Check the arithmetic by independently reviewing the pair-distance multiplicities, radius scaling, and charge dependence; if a continuum approximation is used, explain how it compares.
Report the minimum energy and briefly explain the geometric model and any approximation used.
